elites.name: emergent-world-models-for-science
elites.title: Emergent World Models for Automated Scientific Discovery
elites.short_hypothesis: AI systems that autonomously construct and refine internal world models from raw observational data will be capable of generating novel scientific hypotheses and designing experiments to test them, leading to accelerated discovery across unforeseen scientific domains.
elites.abstract: We propose developing AI agents that move beyond task-specific learning to build comprehensive, dynamic world models from diverse, unstructured data streams. These agents will then leverage their internal understanding of scientific principles to autonomously formulate falsifiable hypotheses and design novel experiments, thereby driving open-ended scientific progress without explicit human guidance on the scientific method itself.

elites.name: recursive-world-model-science
elites.title: Recursive World Model Refinement for Automated Scientific Discovery
elites.short_hypothesis: AI systems capable of autonomously and recursively refining their internal world models will accelerate scientific discovery by enabling more efficient hypothesis generation, experimental design, and data interpretation.
elites.abstract: Future AI systems must move beyond static world models to dynamically update and improve their understanding of the physical and abstract world based on new observations and experimental results. This recursive refinement process, inspired by scientific progress itself, will unlock new avenues for automated scientific discovery by allowing AI to autonomously identify knowledge gaps, propose novel experiments, and interpret complex data with increasing sophistication.

elites.name: emergent_ecosystems_creative_generalization
elites.title: Self-Assembling Scientific Ecosystems for Unforeseen Domain Discovery
elites.short_hypothesis: Artificial life principles will enable AI agents to autonomously form self-organizing scientific ecosystems that can creatively generalize problem-solving to novel domains.
elites.abstract: This research direction proposes the creation of AI systems where agents, inspired by artificial life, autonomously form complex, self-organizing 'ecosystems' to drive scientific discovery. These emergent ecosystems will leverage symbiotic knowledge generation and division of labor to tackle and creatively solve problems in entirely unforeseen domains, transcending the limitations of fixed task categories and human-designed architectures.

elites.name: emergent_ecosystem_quality_diversity
elites.title: Evolutionary Quality-Diversity for Self-Assembling Scientific Ecosystems
elites.short_hypothesis: Applying evolutionary quality-diversity algorithms will enable AI agents to autonomously form diverse, specialized scientific sub-ecosystems that collectively achieve broader and more robust scientific progress than monolithic approaches.
elites.abstract: This research proposes leveraging evolutionary quality-diversity (QD) algorithms to guide the self-assembly of AI agents into distinct scientific 'niches' and sub-ecosystems, each optimized for different research methodologies or problem domains. By promoting diversity in agent capabilities and interaction strategies, these QD-driven ecosystems will unlock novel avenues of scientific discovery and accelerate progress beyond the limitations of current monolithic AI scientist frameworks.
